question: Solving x^2 - 10x + 24 = 0 for the smaller root is 4 m/s. A 52 kg mass has kinetic energy scaled by 4, decreased by 4, scaled by 12, converted to kJ. A rating is 100 m/s. What is the final energy in kJ?

A bead of mass 2 kg slides on a lab-bench rail 0.9 m long. It starts from rest at t = 2 s, and from t = 2 s to t = 3 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 4t² + 5t with t in seconds. Take its energy of motion at its speed at t = 3 s, add 22 J from a magnetic kick, and express the result in kJ. 11 identical beads are run this way, and the experiment is repeated 10 times. What is the total energy over all beads and repeats, in kJ?

The value a technician finally records, in kJ, is 16 kJ less than a subtotal. The subtotal is 25 kJ of battery reserve added to the energy of motion of a 10 kg cart, after that energy has been converted to kJ. The cart moves at a speed in m/s equal to 7 times the greatest common divisor of 351 and 373. The cart's wheels are 12 cm in diameter. What value does the technician record, in kJ?

The total on a dockside crane's load sheet, in kN, is 6 times a per-crane figure. The per-crane figure is 5 kN of wind allowance added to a six-cable total. The six-cable total is 6 times a single-cable force expressed in kN. The single-cable force is what is needed to accelerate a 182,000 g hook block at a rate in m/s² equal to the smaller root of x² - 7x + 10 = 0. What is the total on the load sheet, in kN?

The number the sheet ends on is 22 J less than a figure that is 18 J above a value 8 J below the energy described here. A cam gives the follower displacement as 5 times the cube of the shaft angle minus 4 times the square of the shaft angle, and the rate at which that displacement is changing at a shaft angle of 2.0 is the release speed in metres per second of a slider whose mass is 2 kg. The energy the slider carries because of its motion is the energy in question. The shaft turns at 240 rpm. What number does the sheet end on, in J?

A plant ledger closes with a number that is 12 N more than a figure, and that figure was itself 28 N more than a line total. The line total is 11 times a bay figure, and the bay figure is 12 times the force needed to accelerate one carrier of 191000 grams. The carrier's acceleration in metres per second squared is the largest whole number that divides both 122 and 51 exactly, with nothing left over. The plant floor is 40 m long, a dimension the ledger never uses. What number, in newtons, closes the ledger?

A test range measures a small sabot launched along a rail. The launcher drives the sabot with 2 identical coils, and each coil contributes 8 m/s while it charges and a further 2 m/s while it discharges. A trailing spring then adds another 25 m/s, and the sabot leaves the rail at the accumulated speed. The sabot has a mass of 4000 g. The bench measures the energy it carries by virtue of that motion, subtracts 27 J for the rail friction and a further 26 J for the muzzle seal. What is the bench's corrected reading, in kJ?

A 46000 g sled on a test track 75 m long moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the rate of change of the curve 3x^3 + 2x^2 with respect to x at x = 1. Find the sled's kinetic energy in joules. The track runs 11 identical sleds, so multiply by 11, and subtract 4 J for the energy lost in the starting gate. Convert the result to kilojoules, and then add 16 kJ for the energy stored in the track's launch springs. What is the final figure in kJ?

Integrating 3x^2 + x from 2 to 4 gives an effective velocity (m/s). A 51 kg mass has kinetic energy increased by 17, converted to kJ, increased by 21, and decreased by 2. A maximum thrust of 100 kW is noted but not used. What is the final energy in kJ?
The GCD of 136 and 73 gives acceleration on 57 kg mass (multiplied by 11). Kinetic energy is converted to kJ, scaled by 12 twice, and scaled by 10. What is the final energy in kJ?

Solving x² - 10·x + 21 = 0, smaller root is 3 m/s. After adding 14, get 17 m/s. With 149 kg, force = 2533 N, scaled by 9, increased by 2, converted to kiloNewtons. The wavelength is 650 nm, not relevant. What is the final force in kiloNewtons?

At a pinball launcher test rig, the rate at which the plunger's acceleration builds up -- its jerk, in meters per second cubed -- follows j(t) = 4t^2 + 6t, where t is the time in seconds after release. Engineers need the total acceleration gained between t = 0 and t = 3 seconds. That acceleration acts on a plunger head with a mass of 50 kilograms. (The plunger spring is rated at 200 newtons per meter, a detail that plays no role here.) Find the push this plunger head requires, in newtons, then convert that number into kilonewtons. Add 14 to the result, then multiply what remains by 7, and then by 9. What is the final number, in kilonewtons?

A load profile is found by integrating 3x² + 4x from x = 2 to x = 4 meters. Subtracting 28 from this integral yields an acceleration in m/s². A 95 kg structural element is accelerated at this rate. The resulting force is increased by 28 N from auxiliary support. Adding another 29 N from an additional source gives the final force. What is the final force in N? (The element's length is 5 meters, which is not applied.)

The final number a satellite-thruster engineer logs, in kilojoules, is 19 less than an earlier figure, itself obtained by multiplying a kilojoule reading by 7 after subtracting 5 from it. That kilojoule reading came from converting an energy value, in joules, carried by a 59 kilogram test mass moving at a speed numerically equal to a component's acceleration at a certain instant. That acceleration, in meters per second squared, is how sharply a point's motion is changing at t = 4 seconds, given that its position, in meters, follows s(t) = 2t^3 - 3t^2 for t in seconds since release. What is the final number, in kilojoules?

A pneumatic launcher fires a puck of mass 29000 g. The puck starts from rest at t = 2 s, and from t = 2 s to t = 3 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 4t² + 2t with t in seconds. Take the puck's energy of motion at its speed at t = 3 s. A magazine holds 12 pucks and the launcher has 6 magazines, all fired identically, so scale the energy to 12 pucks and then to 6 magazines. Finally subtract 8 J of latch friction and add 22 J from the compressor's residual charge. What is the resulting energy, in J?
The second derivative of 3x^3 - 5x^2 at x=2 gives acceleration on 187 kg mass. The force is increased by 4 N, reduced by 13 N, then multiplied by 9 and 3. What is the final force in Newtons?
The calculation 6*(8+5) = 78 gives velocity for 32 kg kinetic energy. Energy is reduced by 6 J, scaled by 10, and reduced by 26 J. What is the final energy in Joules?
The derivative of 4x^3 - 6x^2 at x = 2 is 24. Scaling by 3 gives 72 m/s^2. A 52 kg mass produces force, scaled by 3 and 8 and 7. A damping is 1.0. What is the final force in newtons?

The number the crane inspector ultimately writes down is the load rating for the full set of 11 hoist lines, in kilonewtons. Each hoist line carries 10 identical lifting frames, and each frame has a mass of 42000 g and a hook width of 3 m. During the test lift, every frame accelerates upward at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 8 equals zero. Find the net push required on a single frame in newtons, convert it to kilonewtons, multiply by the 10 frames on one line, and add the line's own 9 kN safety allowance. The inspector's rating is that per-line figure multiplied by the 11 lines. What is the rating in kN?

A vehicle proving ground is commissioning a sled drive. The sled's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 5a + 6 = 0. The sled has a mass of 43 kg, and the control room is at 18 degrees C. The drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion, and the commissioning sheet expresses that force in kilonewtons. Each track runs 2 identical sleds, and the ground has 10 identical tracks. What total force, in kN, do the ground's sled drives supply?

A bottling plant accelerates crates of mass 73000 grams along a line 18 m long. Each crate's acceleration in m/s^2 equals the area under the curve y = 2x^2 + 2x between x = 1 and x = 3, and each crate is pushed with the force producing that acceleration. A pusher handles 3 crates, a line has 10 identical pushers, and the line's frame also carries 22 N from a tensioning spring on top of the combined push. The plant runs 8 identical lines. What total force, in N, do the frames of all 8 lines carry?

A suspension system on a 196 kg component is tested with stress values from x² - 9x + 20, selecting the smaller solution (4 m/s²). The acceleration is adjusted by subtracting 3 m/s² to yield 1 m/s². Force is calculated, converted to kN, then reduced by 27 kN for baseline stiffness, and further reduced by 14 kN for damping contribution. The test rig age of 8 years is not used. What is the net suspension force in kN?
Solving x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0 for the smaller root is 1 m/s. A 58 kg mass has kinetic energy scaled by 8 and 7, converted to kJ, scaled by 9. A thermal is 100 C. What is the final energy in kJ?

The final step of this test rig's calculation always multiplies the kilonewton reading by 3 right before it's logged — keep that in mind. A test carriage on a rail rig has a mass of 199 kilograms. The carriage's speed, in meters per second, t seconds after launch, follows the pattern 5 times t squared plus 7 times t; engineers need the total distance the carriage covers between t = 2 seconds and t = 3 seconds, and use that total distance as the carriage's acceleration, in meters per second squared. Using that acceleration and the carriage's mass, a certain force is found. That force, in newtons, is converted into kilonewtons, then multiplied by 7 because seven identical carriages run that test. A calibration offset then subtracts 24. Finally, exactly as noted at the start, the whole total is multiplied by 3. What is the resulting force, in kilonewtons?

A power calculation combines velocity from 3 × (4 + 4) = 24 m/s applied to a 47 kg mass. Kinetic energy is calculated, increased by 21 J for boosting, amplified 4 times through power stages, and increased by 17 J for auxiliary storage. A monitoring frequency of 60 Hz is unused. What is the final stored energy in J?
